title: Pen Test Stakeholder Liaison and Data Minimization Guidelines
body:
Purpose and scope:

This document is a lightweight runbook for coordinating third-party and internal penetration testing at Redwood Inference with a focus on:
- Clear stakeholder liaison during planning and debrief.
- Minimizing sensitive data in evidence packages (PII, secrets).
- Mapping audit-log schema to SIEM exports and automated evidence ingestion.
- RBAC v2 considerations for temporary tester access and revocation.
- Clear findings summary and practical remediation templates with owners and SLAs.

Audience:
- Security & Compliance, Eng leads, SRE, Product security liaisons, Legal/Privacy, Solutions Eng, Third-party vendors conducting assessments.

Pre-engagement checklist (timeline: propose 3–4 weeks before test):
1) Scope & Objectives: define targets (networks, endpoints, APIs, models, datasets), allowed techniques (no destructive injection, no exfil via production customer data unless explicitly approved), and test window.
2) Stakeholder Roster: assign names and contact details for Incident Liaison, Evidence Custodian, SRE on-call, Product Owner, and Legal point-of-contact.
3) Access Model & RBAC: document accounts to be used. Prefer ephemeral test roles with least privilege (RBAC v2 ephemeral tokens).
4) Audit/log visibility validation: verify that audit streams include required fields and that SIEM pipelines are receiving test-plan-specific markers.
5) Data minimization agreement: agree what production data may be touched; if none, identify synthetic datasets or isolated staging targets.
6) Evidence handling and retention policy: agreed retention window (default 90 days for test artifacts unless needed for legal holds).
7) Evidence automation test: run a short smoke test of evidence ingestion (hashing, storage, SIEM indexing) before the engagement.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Liaison (Security lead): triage findings, coordinate with SRE, and talk to vendor.
- Evidence Custodian (SRE or Security Eng): own evidence ingestion storage bucket, ensure encryption-at-rest, run redaction pipeline.
- Product Owner: explain feature behavior and help reproduce issues.
- Legal/Privacy: assess PII risk and legal constraints on evidence storage/transfer.
- Test Vendor Manager: point-of-contact for scheduling and rules of engagement.

RBAC v2 guidelines for tester accounts (practical checklist):
- Create a specific tester role: "pt-test-ephemeral" with time-limited expiration (max 72 hours unless approved).
- Use short-lived credentials only (OAuth/OIDC tokens with lifetime 1–8 hours or temporary AWS/GCP credentials).
- Instrument privilege escalation: any role elevation must be recorded as an auditable workflow (ticket or OAuth grant flow).
- Disable cross-account service tokens; restrict service account key usage during tests.
- After engagement: run automated policy to revoke any outstanding sessions and rotate any credentials that were exposed or used.

Audit log schema and SIEM export mapping (recommended minimal fields):
- audit_timestamp: ISO8601 string (UTC)
- event_id: stable UUID string
- actor_principal: short principal name (user:joe, svc:ingest-worker)
- actor_role: list of roles at the time of event (rbac-v2 role names concatenated)
- action: canonical action name (auth.login, api.generate, storage.read)
- resource_type: e.g., model, dataset, cluster, secret, route
- resource_id: opaque id or path of resource (avoid embedding customer PII there)
- request_id: correlation id from fronting proxies
- src_ip: IP address (obfuscated in evidence packages if needed)
- user_agent: raw UA string
- outcome: success | failure | denied | error
- error_code: internal error code if any
- duration_ms: integer
- kv_cache_hit: boolean (if relevant)
- siem_marker: test_run_id or tag inserted at start of engagement

Note: The audit log must be exportable in newline-delimited JSON to the SIEM with mapping rules to ensure correct field typing in downstream indexes. Provide the siem_marker in the initial test handshake so vendor activity can be filtered/segmented in dashboards.

Example SIEM export notes (textual mapping):
- Map audit_timestamp => @timestamp (date)
- Map actor_principal => actor.id (keyword)
- Map actor_role => actor.roles (keyword array)
- Map action => event.action (keyword)
- Map resource_type/resource_id => resource.* fields (keyword)
- Map outcome/error_code => event.outcome and error.code
- Include test_run_id as a tag to allow queries like "tag:test_run=PT-2025-01"

Evidence automation pipeline (recommended pattern):
1) Capture stage: automated agents (SRE hooks, proxy traces, app audit exporters) write NDJSON to an isolated ingestion bucket with ACL restricted to Evidence Custodian. Prefix with test_run_id.
2) Hashing & manifest: compute sha256 per file and generate a signed manifest.json that lists file paths, sizes, hashes, and capture timestamps.
3) Redaction stage: run configurable redaction rules (PII regexes, key patterns, IP masking) producing redacted copies and an E2E log of redaction operations. Redaction must be reversible only with a documented key and Legal approval; default is irreversible pseudonymization.
4) SIEM Indexing: index raw (if permitted) and redacted streams into SIEM indexes. Always index the manifest and metadata.
5) Evidence packaging: create a signed evidence bundle (manifest + data pointers + hashes + redaction report + timeline).
6) Retention & deletion: run retention job to remove raw unredacted artifacts after the agreed window; keep manifests and redaction reports for audit (90 days default).

Data minimization and PII handling rules:
- Default: do not include production customer PII in evidence. Where unavoidable, prioritize synthetic or redacted copies.
- On-capture tagging: any log containing user identifiers must be tagged and routed to a sensitive index with restricted access.
- Mask IPs in bundles unless required for reproduction; prefer CIDR or city-level aggregation.
- Secrets detection: run automated secret scanning on captured artifacts; any artifact containing secrets must be destroyed and the test paused while rotation occurs.
- Legal holds: if Legal requests raw artifacts for litigation, Evidence Custodian must record chain-of-custody steps and change retention policy per instruction.

Findings summary and remediation template (to be delivered within 3 business days of triage):
- Finding ID: PT-YYYY-NNN
- Title: short summary (1 line)
- Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low | Informational
- Affected assets: list of resource_ids (use internal ids where possible to avoid PII in docs)
- Reproduction steps: concise steps to reproduce (screenshots or minimal repro harness references)
- Observed behavior: what happened (with references to audit events: event_id(s))
- Root cause hypothesis: short statement
- Immediate mitigations (if any): e.g., block rule, temporary config change, revoke role
- Recommended remediations: 1) fix, 2) verification plan (tests/eval), 3) rollback plan if needed
- Owner: name, team, pager or contact
- ETA: target completion date
- Post-fix verification: which tests to run and which audit fields to check
- Closure criteria: evidence manifest + SIEM events + unit/integration test results

Remediation cadence guidance (suggested):
- Critical: notify exec on-call + 72 hour remediation window with daily progress updates
- High: 14 day remediation with cadence twice weekly
- Medium: 45 day remediation with weekly updates
- Low: 90 day backlog grooming and triage

Evidence release & redaction approval flow (operational):
1) Evidence Custodian prepares candidate bundle and redaction report.
2) Security lead and Product Owner review; Legal signs off on any retained PII.
3) Vendor receives redacted bundle via secure transfer (S3 presigned URL with short TTL or secure file share).
4) If vendor requires additional detail, request must go back through Incident Liaison with justification; escalate to Legal for PII exceptions.

Post-engagement checklist (what to run immediately after test):
- Revoke all ephemeral tester roles and rotate any credentials used during the test.
- Run integrity checks: verify manifest hashes for all evidence artifacts and store manifest in immutable archive.
- Run secret scan and validate no secrets leaked into vendor share.
- Publish anonymized executive summary (one page) for leadership with high-level findings and next steps.
- Schedule a 2-week follow-up to validate remediations and replay selected test cases in staging.

Appendix: Useful command snippets (examples):
- Generate manifest (example): sha256sum $(ls /tmp/evidence/*.ndjson) > manifest.sha256
- Sample filter to extract PT run in logs: jq 'select(.siem_marker == "PT-2025-01")' /var/log/audit.ndjson | head -n 200
- Revoke sessions (example pseudo): curl -X POST https://idp.internal/auth/revoke -d '{"user":"pt-tester-123"}'

Common failure modes & mitigations (observed in prior engagements):
- Missing siem_marker: add a test preflight step that injects marker events and check for indexing.
- Evidence store ACL misconfig: use automated IAM policy templates and run pre-engagement verification.
- Over-collection of PII: require Product Owner sign-off before any production data extraction and prefer synthetic data.
- Unrevoked sessions: add automated post-test revoke job and an audit that runs within 30 minutes of engagement end.

Contact & escalation:
- Primary Security Liaison: Aisha Patel (pager: sec-oncall)
- Evidence Custodian: Marco Hernandez (sre-team)
- Legal privacy: Lin Zhou (legal@redwood.ai)
- If exec escalation required: CTO on-call

Document notes:
- This is intentionally prescriptive and intended to make pen test coordination lower friction while protecting customer data.
- Keep this document updated with anonymized post-mortem notes after each engagement so runbook sharpens over time.
